newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH JUNE UNEMPLOYMENT DATA BETTER THAN EXPECTED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH JUNE UNEMPLOYMENT DATA BETTER THAN EXPECTED.

text.p: Poland's June jobless data proved better than expected showing unemployment rate falling 0.1 point to 11.6 percent despite a seasonal jump in registrations of school graduates, the labour minister said.

"Usually in June the unemployment rate rose as scores of graduates enlisted in labour offices' registries. We were afraid the the rate would go up in June," Tadeusz Zielinski told a news conference on Friday.
He said that 50,000 graduates registered with employment offices last month against 73,000 in 1996 and 189,000 in 1995.
National Labour Office President Andrzej Pilat, also present, said all jobless from flooded regions in southern Poland would be hired for public reconstruction works in the area.
"All labour offices in this region were instructed to guide every applying jobless person for public works. This will temporarily reduce unemployment there," Pilat said.
